input.summary: The packet contains a synthetic networking claim about the effect of 20 ms added delay on TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. The user raises a unit ambiguity: the paper reportedly states a threshold of 0.2 seconds, while a personal note says 0.2 milliseconds. These differ by a factor of 1000 and represent very different detection sensitivities. Neither value can be verified from the provided metadata alone (no full text, no table, no figure reference is available). The proposed experiment uses the emulated-netem-v1 runner to measure flow completion time (FCT) in milliseconds across two delay conditions (0 ms and 20 ms added one-way delay) under a fixed bottleneck, so that the observed FCT difference can be compared against both candidate thresholds. The unit question must be resolved by the owner before the protocol is frozen; the design below treats both thresholds as candidate falsification bounds and flags the ambiguity explicitly.
questions: The paper states a threshold of 0.2 — is the correct unit seconds (200 ms) or milliseconds (0.2 ms)? Please cite the exact sentence, table, or figure from the source (sha256: aaaa…aaaa) that contains this value so the falsification bound can be set correctly.

What bottleneck rate (Mbit/s), buffer size (kbytes), CCA, and file size (MBytes) does the paper use for its fixed emulated bottleneck conditions? These are required to reproduce the claimed operating point.
Is the 0.2-unit threshold a minimum detectable difference, a reported mean difference, or a statistical significance bound (e.g., a p-value cutoff or confidence-interval half-width)?

proposal.problem: A synthetic networking paper claims that adding 20 ms one-way delay changes TCP flow completion time (FCT) under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. The magnitude of the change is described with a threshold value of '0.2', but the unit is disputed: the paper reportedly says seconds (0.2 s = 200 ms) while a user note says milliseconds (0.2 ms). The two values differ by a factor of 1000 and lead to entirely different falsification criteria. No full text or figure is available to resolve the ambiguity from metadata alone.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms one-way delay produce a change in TCP FCT that exceeds 0.2 seconds (200 ms), or 0.2 milliseconds (0.2 ms), and which threshold is consistent with the paper's claim?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two delay conditions are tested: (A) baseline — 0 ms added one-way delay; (B) treatment — 20 ms added one-way delay. All other parameters (bottleneck rate, buffer, CCA, file size) are held fixed. Proposed defaults pending owner confirmation: bottleneck 10 Mbit/s, buffer 128 kbytes, CCA cubic, file size 10 MBytes, 0% loss. Both candidate thresholds (0.2 s and 0.2 ms) are evaluated as separate falsification bounds.
proposal.related_work: Source citation: 'Synthetic networking paper claim for development evaluation' (sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa). Review status: retrieved-unreviewed. No full text provided; coverage is recorded metadata only. The unit ambiguity (seconds vs. milliseconds) cannot be resolved from available metadata.
proposal.alternatives: 1. The true threshold is 0.2 seconds (200 ms): plausible for large files or low-bandwidth bottlenecks where RTT inflation dominates. 2. The true threshold is 0.2 milliseconds (0.2 ms): plausible only if the claim refers to a sub-millisecond precision metric or a statistical bound, not a raw FCT difference. 3. The '0.2' figure refers to a normalized ratio or fraction, not an absolute time — this would require a different metric entirely. 4. The paper uses a different delay value or a different dependent variable than FCT.
proposal.design: Pilot experiment using the emulated-netem-v1 runner. Two client flows are run under each of the two delay conditions (0 ms and 20 ms). FCT is recorded in milliseconds for each flow. The mean FCT difference (treatment minus baseline) is computed and compared against both candidate thresholds: 200 ms (0.2 s) and 0.2 ms. Replications: 16 per condition (8 per condition per client, interleaved). Proposed bottleneck: 10 Mbit/s, 128 kbytes buffer, cubic CCA, 10 MBytes file, 0% loss. Owner must confirm or override bottleneck parameters and resolve the unit question before the protocol is frozen. This is a pilot; causal or generalizing conclusions are not warranted from a single emulated pilot.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms (milliseconds). Derived metric: mean FCT difference between 20 ms delay condition and 0 ms baseline condition, in milliseconds. Both candidate falsification bounds are evaluated: (i) |ΔFCT| > 200 ms (0.2 s threshold); (ii) |ΔFCT| > 0.2 ms (0.2 ms threshold).
proposal.controls: Fixed across all runs: bottleneck rate, buffer size, CCA, file size, loss percentage (0%), number of clients (2), snapshot interval (100 ms). The only varied factor is added one-way client delay (0 ms vs. 20 ms). No other network parameters are changed between conditions.
proposal.falsification: The claim is not supported in this pilot if the observed mean FCT difference between the 20 ms delay condition and the 0 ms baseline is zero or negligible under both candidate thresholds. Specifically: (i) If |ΔFCT| ≤ 200 ms, the 0.2-second threshold is not exceeded; (ii) If |ΔFCT| ≤ 0.2 ms, the 0.2-millisecond threshold is not exceeded. Because the unit is unresolved, both bounds are evaluated and reported separately. A pilot result cannot establish causality or generalization. The unit ambiguity must be resolved by the owner using the original source before a definitive falsification rule is applied.
proposal.inputs: Required: paper source sha256 = aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa (full text not available; unit ambiguity unresolved). Packet sha256 = a1b401caab0920ee2f11377b7285ff0ef7269c187cfa7f3df1c1cb576ba8c0da. Proposed emulated config: num_clients=2, client_delays_ms=[0,20] (one condition per run), client_ccas=[cubic,cubic], client_file_sizes_mbytes=[10,10], loss_pct=0, snapshot_interval_ms=100, script=netem_nines.py, bottleneck_all_client_rate_mbit=10, bottleneck_buffer_kbytes=128. Owner must confirm bottleneck parameters and resolve the 0.2 s vs. 0.2 ms unit question.
proposal.limitations: 1. Unit ambiguity (seconds vs. milliseconds) is unresolved; the falsification criterion cannot be finalized without owner clarification. 2. No full text is available; the paper's exact bottleneck configuration, CCA, and file size are unknown — proposed defaults may not reproduce the paper's operating point. 3. This is an emulated (not real-world) pilot; results may not generalize to physical networks. 4. Only 2 clients and 1 bottleneck topology are tested. 5. Pilot success does not establish causality or broader validity. 6. Fresh AI reviews share models and inputs and are not independent human review.

What are the paper's bottleneck rate (Mbit/s), buffer (kbytes), CCA, and file size (MBytes)?

protocol.hypotheses: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.

metrics.name: flow_completion_time_ms
metrics.criterion: Mean FCT difference (20 ms delay minus 0 ms baseline) evaluated against both 200 ms and 0.2 ms thresholds

protocol.dates_or_epochs: To be assigned at owner adoption; no prior exposure to treatment results.
protocol.seeds: Not applicable for deterministic netem emulation; replications provide variability estimate.

sensitivity.rationale: The falsification criterion is highly sensitive to the unit choice (factor of 1000). Bottleneck rate and file size also strongly affect absolute FCT; owner must confirm these before interpreting results against the paper's threshold.

protocol.replication_unit: per-configuration run (both clients measured per run)
protocol.sample_size_rationale: 16 replications per configuration (32 total) provides a descriptive range of FCT variability in the emulated environment within the 32-replication pilot limit. Inferential intervals are not declared without a justified independent sampling design.
protocol.exclusions: Runs with missing or zero FCT records for any client are excluded and flagged.
protocol.missing_data: If FCT records are missing for a run, that run is excluded; the remaining runs are analyzed and the exclusion count is reported.
protocol.statistics: Descriptive: mean and range of FCT per configuration; mean FCT difference (treatment minus baseline). Both candidate thresholds (200 ms and 0.2 ms) are evaluated as binary criteria. No inferential intervals are declared; this is a pilot.
protocol.dependence: Replications within the same emulated session may share system state; treated as descriptive range, not independent samples. Temporal ordering of runs is recorded.

resource_limits.cost_basis: Emulated runner; no cloud cost model available.

protocol.stopping_rule: All 32 planned runs are completed unless a configuration produces zero valid FCT records, in which case the run is flagged and excluded. No adaptive stopping based on interim results.
protocol.prior_exposure: No prior measurements have been reported for this packet.
protocol.coverage_limits: Emulated single-bottleneck topology only; 1 CCA (cubic); 1 file size; 2 clients. Results do not generalize to other topologies, CCAs, or real-world networks.
protocol.data_origin: Emulated network (netem-v1 runner); not real-world traffic.
